title: Costa Rica vs Colombia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Costa Rica and Colombia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, wildlife, coffee culture, and traveler preferences.

faqs.question: Is Costa Rica or Colombia cheaper?
faqs.answer: Colombia is significantly cheaper — roughly 2-3x less expensive. A mid-range day in Colombia runs $40-70 USD; Costa Rica runs $100-160 USD. faqs.answer: Costa Rica's dry season (December–April) is ideal for most tourist areas. The Pacific coast is best January–April; Caribbean coast flips with a different wet/dry season. faqs.question: Is Costa Rica or Colombia better for first-time Latin America visitors?
faqs.answer: Costa Rica is often recommended for first-timers: it's straightforward, English is widely spoken in tourist areas, infrastructure is excellent, and it feels safer and more streamlined. faqs.question: Can you visit both Costa Rica and Colombia in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes, though they're not as close as they look on a map. Direct flights between San José (Costa Rica) and Bogotá, Medellín, or Cartagena run 2-3 hours and can be found for $100-200 one-way on Avianca, Copa, or LATAM. A 3-week itinerary covering both is very doable and popular on r/solotravel.

faqs.question: Which is better for surfing, Costa Rica or Colombia?
faqs.answer: Costa Rica is the superior surf destination. Santa Teresa, Nosara, Pavones, Tamarindo, and Jaco all have world-class waves for various levels. Colombia has decent surf (Nuquí, Capurganá, Palomino on the Caribbean) but is not in the same league for dedicated surfers.
